subject: internship
name: Internship
exam: TU assessment: 60% final examination set by the university, 40% internal (assignments, lab work, attendance). Confirm the split in your college's notice.

units.title: The Internship: Purpose, Placement Search, CV and Interview
topics: The CV, the email and the interview
Eight reasons good students lose good placements

sections.title: The CV, the email and the interview
Eight reasons good students lose good placements

summary: An internship is work in someone else's problem space, supervised and assessed; it differs from a project, a course and a job.
Write three SMART learning objectives before searching; they decide whether an offer is good.
Compare at least three options with a weighted matrix and check the result with a sensitivity test.
The CV is one page and proof-first; the email is short and specific; the interview uses honest STAR stories.
Start the search twelve weeks before the placement and finish the paperwork three weeks before.

units.title: Workplace Conduct: First Day, Etiquette, Confidentiality and Safety
topics: The first day and the first week
Eight habits that make an intern trusted

sections.title: The first day and the first week
Eight habits that make an intern trusted

summary: The first week is a checklist; confirm in week one that real tasks match your objectives.
Good communication means the right channel, a complete message and a record of decisions.
Use the 15-minute rule to balance independence with asking for help.
Information has four levels; restricted data (passwords, IDs) never lives in code or chat.
A leaked secret must be changed, not just deleted, and reported immediately.
You have rights to a clear agreement, respect and safety; use your coordinator if they are not met.

units.title: Working the Weeks: Learning Plan, Daily Log and Weekly Review
topics: Eight rules for a log that passes a supervisor's eye

sections.title: Eight rules for a log that passes a supervisor's eye

summary: Plan the placement as observe, contribute, own, hand over and share the plan with your supervisor.
A daily log has six fields; the entry must be specific, same-day and truthful.
The weekly review (Keep, Stop, Try) keeps the placement on track and produces the supervisor's signature.
Log data can be analysed: in the example, coding 34 percent, learning 19, and one honest miss against L3.
Never adjust the log to fit the objective; adjust the objective next time and explain the gap.

units.title: Technical Contribution: Tickets, Code Review, Testing and Hand-over
topics: Reading a code base you did not write
Fix, test and ask for review
What a code review looks for
Eight practices of interns whose work gets merged

sections.title: Reading a code base you did not write
Fix, test and ask for review
What a code review looks for
Eight practices of interns whose work gets merged

summary: A ticket moves from backlog to deployed, and somebody else sees it at every step.
Read an unfamiliar code base by running it, finding the entry point, tracing one path and asking one precise question.
Reproduce first: HD-31 failed on 2 of 4 invoices because float 0.565 rounds down; Decimal rounding once gives 55.26.
Tests (6 of 6 passing) prove the fix and document the promise; edge cases matter.
Code review is normal, expected and educational; reply to every comment.
A hand-over page makes the work usable after you leave.

units.title: Report, Presentation and Viva: Proving What You Did and Learned
topics: The viva: twelve questions and model answers
Eight habits that finish an internship well

sections.title: The viva: twelve questions and model answers
Eight habits that finish an internship well

summary: The report is specific, evidence-based and honest; chapters 4 and 5 (your work) carry the most pages.
Use a page budget, write from week five and cite log dates and ticket numbers.
Reflect with a before-and-after self-assessment: mean 2.25 to 4.00 in the example, with one weak skill named.
Request certificate, evaluation and reference early; thank people.
A ten-minute talk tells one story; the viva rewards claim, evidence and an honest limit.
